variants.headline: Looking back: party divides in two
variants.sub: A split in {party} has produced the new party {splinter}.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The party {party} had split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party.

Workers deserve political organisations that take their interests seriously, whether those organisations stand together or apart. A split should be judged with that purpose in mind. Labour gains little from celebrating an internal victory if the question of a decent working life disappears behind the competing party labels.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We judge {target} harshly in this matter. Political organisation carries obligations beyond the comfort of its leaders, and division is an appropriate occasion to question the quality of that stewardship.

variants.headline: Looking back: a political organisation breaks apart
variants.sub: The new party {splinter} has broken away from {party}.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: A split in {party} had produced the new party {splinter}.

Workers deserve political organisations that take their interests seriously, whether those organisations stand together or apart. A split should be judged with that purpose in mind. Labour gains little from celebrating an internal victory if the question of a decent working life disappears behind the competing party labels.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We judge {target} harshly in this matter. Political organisation carries obligations beyond the comfort of its leaders, and division is an appropriate occasion to question the quality of that stewardship.

variants.headline: Looking back: unity gives way to a party split
variants.sub: The party {party} has split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: The new party {splinter} had broken away from {party}.

Workers deserve political organisations that take their interests seriously, whether those organisations stand together or apart. A split should be judged with that purpose in mind. Labour gains little from celebrating an internal victory if the question of a decent working life disappears behind the competing party labels.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We judge {target} harshly in this matter. Political organisation carries obligations beyond the comfort of its leaders, and division is an appropriate occasion to question the quality of that stewardship.
